title: "WRF Meteorological Drivers"

```{r}
#| include: false
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE)
```

## Purpose

This guide describes how to convert hourly WRF output from the Cal-Adapt
Analytics Engine into CF-1.8 NetCDF meteorological driver files. The workflow
is intended for site-based ecosystem models and other tools that consume
CF-standard meteorological forcing.

`caladaptaer` provides three export paths:

- `cae_write_cf_netcdf()` writes a CF NetCDF file from a named list of WRF
  `stars` grids.
- `cae_build_reanalysis_drivers()` streams UCLA's ERA5-driven WRF reanalysis files.
- `cae_build_met_drivers()` extracts WRF data for multiple sites and writes one
  NetCDF file per site per year.

## Prerequisites

Install `caladaptaer` and verify that GDAL is available as described in
[Getting Started](getting_started.qmd). This guide assumes the package is
already installed.

```{r}
library(caladaptaer)
```

The driver workflow requires WRF hourly data. LOCA2-Hybrid daily products do
not provide the full hourly meteorological variable set required by these
functions.

## Required Inputs

Multi-site driver generation requires a site table with three columns:

| Column | Description |
|---|---|
| `site_id` | Site identifier used in output paths |
| `lon` | Longitude in WGS84 decimal degrees |
| `lat` | Latitude in WGS84 decimal degrees |

Additional columns can be present; `cae_build_met_drivers()` uses only
`site_id`, `lon`, and `lat`.

```{r}
sites <- data.frame(
    site_id = c("fresno", "los_angeles", "sacramento"),
    lon = c(-119.77, -118.24, -121.49),
    lat = c(36.75, 34.05, 38.58)
)
```

Driver generation also requires a WRF model, scenario, year range, spatial
grid, and output directory. Use `cae_models()`, `cae_scenarios()`, and
`cae_search()` to confirm availability before starting a large job.

## Required Variables

The CF driver files are built from eight WRF surface meteorology variables.
`wind_speed` is derived from `u10` and `v10`.

| CF variable | WRF variable | WRF units | CF units | Conversion |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `air_temperature` | `t2` | K | K | none |
| `air_pressure` | `psfc` | Pa | Pa | none |
| `precipitation_flux` | `prec` | mm per timestep | kg m-2 s-1 | divide by timestep seconds |
| `specific_humidity` | `q2` | kg kg-1 mixing ratio | 1 | `q2 / (1 + q2)` |
| `surface_downwelling_shortwave_flux_in_air` | `swdnb` | W m-2 | W m-2 | none |
| `surface_downwelling_longwave_flux_in_air` | `lwdnb` | W m-2 | W m-2 | none |
| `eastward_wind` | `u10` | m s-1 | m s-1 | none |
| `northward_wind` | `v10` | m s-1 | m s-1 | none |
| `wind_speed` | `u10`, `v10` | m s-1 | m s-1 | `sqrt(u10^2 + v10^2)` |

Use `cae_check_variables()` to check whether the required variables are present
or derivable for a model, scenario, timescale, and resolution.

```{r}
cae_check_variables(
    model = "CESM2",
    scenario = "ssp370",
    timescale = "1hr",
    resolution = "d01"
)
```

Some WRF models store precipitation as accumulated convective and
non-convective components rather than the precomputed `prec` field.
`caladaptaer` derives `prec` from those components when possible.

## Single-Grid Workflow

Use `cae_write_cf_netcdf()` when the intended output is a CF NetCDF file for a
single WRF grid subset. The input is a named list of `stars` objects, one per
required WRF variable.

```{r}
wrf_vars <- c("t2", "psfc", "prec", "q2", "swdnb", "lwdnb", "u10", "v10")

var_data <- lapply(wrf_vars, function(variable) {
    cae_fetch(
        variable = variable,
        model = "CESM2",
        scenario = "ssp370",
        timescale = "1hr",
        resolution = "d01",
        start_time = "2050-07-01T00:00:00",
        end_time = "2050-07-01T23:00:00"
    )
})
names(var_data) <- wrf_vars

cae_write_cf_netcdf(
    var_list = var_data,
    outfile = "CESM2.ssp370.2050-07-01.cf.nc",
    dt_seconds = 3600,
    overwrite = TRUE
)
```

The output file contains CF-1.8 / ACDD-1.3 metadata, CF variable names, converted
units, and derived wind speed.

## Multi-Site Workflow

Use `cae_build_met_drivers()` when the intended output is one NetCDF file per
site per year. The function retrieves unique native cells in bounded batches,
shares weather among sites in the same cell, and writes site-year files.

```{r}
result <- cae_build_met_drivers(
    sites = sites,
    model = "CESM2",
    scenario = "ssp370",
    start_year = 2050,
    end_year = 2051,
    outdir = "met_drivers",
    resolution = "d01"
)

head(result)
```

By default, completed files are validated before reuse. Files with incompatible
requests, coordinates, variables, or time axes are regenerated. Set
`overwrite = TRUE` to regenerate matching files as well.

```{r}
result <- cae_build_met_drivers(
    sites = sites,
    model = "CESM2",
    scenario = "ssp370",
    start_year = 2050,
    end_year = 2051,
    outdir = "met_drivers",
    resolution = "d01",
    overwrite = TRUE
)
```

## Output Structure

`cae_build_met_drivers()` writes files using this path pattern:

```text
{outdir}/{site_id}/{model}.{scenario}.{year}.nc
```

For example:

```text
met_drivers/fresno/CESM2.ssp370.2050.nc
met_drivers/los_angeles/CESM2.ssp370.2050.nc
met_drivers/sacramento/CESM2.ssp370.2050.nc
```

Each file contains one site and one year of hourly data. Dimensions are
`latitude`, `longitude`, and `time`. The time coordinate retains the source encoding and calendar. Missing source
values remain missing; absent leap days remain absent.


## Bulk access and local caching

Add `cache_dir = "source-cache"` to stage only the requested Zarr chunks and
reuse them across batches and runs; omit it for direct remote reads. Set
`batch_size` to bound the number of unique cells held together in memory
(default 64). A local store or named list of variable-to-store paths can be
passed through `source`. Full annual coverage is checked against native source
timestamps, allowing an entirely absent February 29 but no other missing hours.
Mismatched variable time axes fail rather than being aligned silently.

```{r}
# A full-year export; start with a small site set.
result <- cae_build_met_drivers(sites, "CESM2", "ssp370", 2024, 2024,
    "met_drivers", resolution = "d03", cache_dir = "source-cache",
    batch_size = 16L)
```

## UCLA ERA5-driven WRF reanalysis files

These APIs currently support UCLA's ERA5-driven WRF reanalysis only. They do not
retrieve GCM historical simulations or other reanalysis products.
Cataloged WRF-ERA5 Zarr coverage may end before the direct reanalysis files.
List the requested period and one preceding hour before exporting a full year:

```{r}
files <- cae_reanalysis_files("2022-12-31 23:00:00", "2023-12-31 23:00:00", "d03")
result <- cae_build_reanalysis_drivers(sites, files, 2023, 2023,
    outdir = "reanalysis_drivers", cache_dir = "reanalysis_sources",
    resolution = "d03", retain_source = FALSE, batch_size = 16L)
```

This is a full-year download, not a small tutorial fetch. Inspect file sizes and
coverage first. `retain_source = TRUE` (default) keeps newly downloaded sources.
FALSE downloads into owned temporary directories and discards each file only
after all requested cells have been read. Pre-existing cache files are always
preserved. The reanalysis reader streams into temporary output files rather
than holding an annual array for every site. It trades additional output I/O
for bounded memory and source storage.

Internal WRF `Times` values are the exported timestamps. Filenames may identify
a nominal hour a few seconds earlier; `source_nominal_time` retains those nominal
times separately. `precipitation_time` retains the precipitation source endpoint
when it differs at a run boundary; `time_bounds` records its intervals, including
the preceding source timestamp. Integrate `precipitation_flux` against those
interval lengths, rather than assuming every interval is exactly 3,600 seconds.
Accumulation handling uses the preceding record and, at overlapping September
run boundaries, the previous run's final counter before adopting the new baseline.

Outputs reference an immutable JSON source manifest under `source-manifests/`.
Keep that directory with the exported dataset. A checksum connects each file to
its source listing. Restarting validates existing outputs before reuse; a failed
write leaves no new final output file, while previously completed files remain.

## Calendars, provenance, and downstream models

CF exports preserve native calendar coordinates and source missingness. They do
not interpolate leap days, create synthetic precipitation, or fill missing data.
A downstream model may require different calendars or formats; those decisions
are outside caladaptaer. For no-leap sources affected by the former arithmetic
time-indexing bug, regenerate the exports.

Both grid and site files record `CF-1.8, ACDD-1.3`, source identifiers, catalog
applicability, model/scenario/member, variables, resolution, requested period,
actual coverage, source calendar/time units, and conversion history. Unknown
caller metadata is labeled explicitly. Local staging preserves original remote
source identity. See `inst/benchmarks/` in the source package for bounded access
comparisons; their timings are not full-year production estimates.
